content.text: repete uma palavra da fala com outro sentido. 🎧
“Can you give me a hand with these boxes?”
responde como se fosse outra coisa. 🎧
🎧 > “I was wondering if you had a minute to look at my résumé.”
a) I have a minute, it's 3:01. ✘ (literal)
b) Sure, I'm free now. Let's see it. ✔
4.1 Troque e fale: aceitar e recusar
I'm afraid I can't right now — maybe later?
O professor faz pedidos; o aluno alterna aceitar e recusar com uma razão:
Could you lend me your notes? · Would you mind switching seats? · Do you think you could cover my shift? · Can you help me move on Saturday?
4.2 Diga a intenção escondida e responda
🎧 1. “This box is way too heavy for me.”
🎧 2. “The deadline is tomorrow and I haven't even started.”
🎧 4. “Sorry — the first or the second floor?”
🎧 a) “Why don't you ask the professor?” b) “Why didn't you ask the professor?”
Pratique: o professor fala uma das duas versões aleatoriamente para 4 situações; o aluno responde de acordo.

content.text: 🎧 Cada fala uma vez. Resposta em até 10 segundos. Depois, o aluno fala a resposta em voz alta.
“Would you mind turning the music down?” — a) Not at all, sorry! b) Yes, I like music. c) It's a new song.
“How about studying at my place tonight?” — a) About two hours. b) Sounds good. What time? c) I studied last night.
“I'm not sure what the professor meant by 'peer review'.” — a) It's when classmates check each other's work. b) The professor is sure. c) I reviewed it.
“You might want to leave early — there's a lot of traffic.” — a) Thanks, I'll go now. b) I want to leave traffic. c) Traffic is early.
“Do you think you could cover my shift on Friday?” — a) I think so too. b) I'm afraid I can't — I'm traveling. c) The shift is on Friday.
“So you're saying the exam is open-book?” — a) Yes, you can use your notes. b) I'm saying hello. c) The book is open.
“Have you thought about applying for the internship?” — a) I'm thinking about lunch. b) Actually, I sent my application yesterday. c) The internship thought.
“I can't hear the speaker from back here.” — a) Let's move closer. b) The speaker is loud. c) I'm here.
“Maybe you should talk to your advisor.” — a) My advisor talks a lot. b) That's a good idea. I'll email her. c) Maybe.
“I'd rather not go out tonight.” — a) OK, let's stay in then. b) Rather is a word. c) Go out now.
o professor repete 1, 2, 5, 7 e 9. O aluno cria uma resposta diferente para cada (aceitar ↔ recusar).
[ ] Diferenciou sugestão de pergunta de motivo?

Para 5 falas da aula, escreva 1 resposta certa + 2 distratores (eco e função errada).
